age.evidence: Adult male (n = 12) and female (n = 12) Sprague-Dawley rats, approximately 100 days of age... In a separate study, male (n =8) and female (n = 8) Sprague-Dawley rats were obtained from Charles River Laboratories (Wilmington, MA) on post-natal day (PND) 70.

sex.evidence: Adult male (n = 12) and female (n = 12) Sprague-Dawley rats... In a separate study, male (n =8) and female (n = 8) Sprague-Dawley rats

dosing.evidence: Mescaline was prepared in sterile saline (0.9% NaCl) for a dose of 50 mg/kg. ... Thirty minutes following injections, animals were placed into the unlit startle chamber for testing.

handling.evidence: No experimenter handling protocol described; only room acclimation and startle-chamber habituation are mentioned.

group_housing.evidence: Animals were housed by sex in Plexiglas cages (two per cage)

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were maintained on a reverse L-D cycle with lights off at 09:00 AM and studied during the dark phase when they are normally active. ... Testing occurred in the dark phase under red light conditions.

assays.assay_description: Rats tested individually in Med Associates sound-attenuated startle chambers (internal animal holder, grid rod floor, load-cell platform) 30 min after mescaline (50 mg/kg) or vehicle. 1-min acclimation, then 40 trials (24 prepulse trials: 70 dB tone at 4, 12 or 20 kHz 100 ms before 100 dB white noise; 16 pulse-alone trials), then 15 noise bursts of 70/80/90 dB (3-8 s ITI). Startle amplitude and % PPI per prepulse frequency measured.

application_type.evidence: Thirty minutes following injections, animals were placed into the unlit startle chamber for testing. (Injection route not stated.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Twenty-four hours prior to testing, animals were weighed, acclimated to the testing room for 20 minutes, and habituated to the startle chamber for 7 minutes with the apparatus turned on.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in foam-lined sound-attenuated startle chambers, which contained an internal animal holder with a grid rod floor on a startle platform

food_restriction.evidence: No food in startle chamber during testing (standard apparatus); home cage food ad libitum: 'Food and water were provided ad libitum.'

water_restriction.evidence: No water in startle chamber during testing (standard apparatus); home cage water ad libitum.

time_to_assay.evidence: Thirty minutes following injections, animals were placed into the unlit startle chamber for testing.

sample_size.evidence: In a separate study, male (n =8) and female (n = 8) Sprague-Dawley rats were obtained from Charles River Laboratories (Wilmington, MA) on post-natal day (PND) 70.

outcomes.summary: Mescaline (50 mg/kg) had frequency-dependent effects on PPI: enhanced at 4 kHz (+27.6%) and 20 kHz (+27.3%) but impaired at 12 kHz (-16.4%) relative to vehicle, an inverted-U frequency profile. Startle amplitude was reduced at 4 kHz (P=0.037) with a trend at 20 kHz; no main effect of treatment.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA: Treatment F=2.97, P=0.091; Frequency F=2.48, P=0.095; Treatment x Frequency F=3.874, P=0.028, ω²=0.098. Independent t-tests: 4 kHz P=0.037; 20 kHz P=0.051; 12 kHz n.s.
outcomes.evidence: a significant Treatment x Frequency interaction (F = 3.874, P = 0.028) and medium effect size (ω 2 = 0.098)... The 4 kHz and 20 kHz intensities enhanced mescaline PPI by +27.6% and +27.3%, respectively, compared to vehicle treatment. The 12 kHz frequency impaired mescaline PPI by -16.4% relative to vehicle.

B1_num_measures.evidence: mescaline significantly reduced the startle amplitude of 4 kHz (P = 0.037)... enhanced mescaline PPI by +27.6% and +27.3% (startle amplitude and % PPI)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: No within-session time-course analysis reported; data analyzed with repeated measures two-way ANOVA across frequencies.

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle magnitude is not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Rats were placed in foam-lined sound-attenuated startle chambers (individual testing).

B6_cognitive.evidence: PPI is a sensorimotor gating reflex measure, not a learned task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Data was collected via the PPI program within the Startle Reflex Package (SOF-826, Med Associates Inc, St. Albans, VT).

B8_multivariate.evidence: The data were analyzed with a repeated measures two-way ANOVA.

E1_environment_type.evidence: startle reflex hardware package (MED-ASR-PRO1, Med Associates Inc, St. Albans, VT)

E3_bedding.evidence: internal animal holder with a grid rod floor

E6_spatial.evidence: single internal animal holder within startle chamber

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were placed in foam-lined sound-attenuated startle chambers

D2_session_duration.evidence: Total session duration not explicitly stated (1-min acclimation, 40 trials, 15 noise bursts with 3-8-s ITI); scored 0 per rubric.

judge_notes: All candidates identified a single behavioural assay (PPI); pharmacological fMRI, resting-state connectivity, and odor-provocation BOLD imaging were excluded as imaging-only readouts without a behavioural task.
Age: two cohorts (fMRI ~100 days; PPI PND70); reported as adult with range 70-100 days. Sex n's summed across both cohorts (20 M, 20 F).
D2: session duration never explicitly stated; scored 0 with low confidence per rubric rule (candidates qwen/gemma inferred <15 min, deepseek flagged not reported).
B1 set to 2-3 (startle amplitude and % PPI), matching modal score of 1; gemma's value label '1' corrected.
Injection route never stated in the paper; application_type and dosing route kept as not_reported.
n_per_group_min left null: allocation of the 16 PPI rats to vehicle vs mescaline groups is not reported.
